description:
Describe only visible facts in the six labeled images. Describe INITIAL and CURRENT separately, without assuming that a CURRENT object retains its INITIAL shape or name. Focus on three things:
1. Task-relevant objects: count, overall shape and thickness, open/closed structure, and distinctive visible features. Color alone does not establish identity.
2. Visible robot/gripper appearance: fingers, links, attachment and opening. Describe only visible parts; cropping or occlusion does not itself mean deformation.
3. Spatial relations: left/right, above/below, inside/outside, stacking and visible support. Distinguish overlap from placement; say when the relation is unclear.
Do not decide task success or consistency, and do not infer motion. Keep observations concise and cite the views. Use neutral geometry when identity is unclear. A hidden feature is not necessarily absent.
Return ONLY JSON with initial and current lists. Each fact has id (I1... or C1...), category (object, relation, robot, or occlusion), text, and views (head, wrist_left, wrist_right). IDs must be unique. Each observation must include object, relation and robot facts; explicitly state when not visible. No verdict. Aim for at most 500 English words total.
judgment:
Compare INITIAL and CURRENT using the original six images and the fallible descriptions. Focus on object appearance, visible robot appearance, and the instructed spatial relation.
Evaluate the four checks independently:
objects_consistent: compare count, shape/thickness, open/closed structure and distinctive visible features of the instructed objects and targets. Matching color or position cannot excuse a clear structural change. Allow supported perspective, rotation, lighting and occlusion differences; use uncertain when critical appearance cannot be compared.
robot_structure_consistent: check visible fingers, links and attachment for clear structural contradictions. Do not reject merely because parts are cropped or hidden; do not invent hidden anatomy.
goal_satisfied: evaluate only the task rule's target placement/spatial relation. Do not put object identity, robot appearance or release requirements into this field; assess those separately. Do not invent additional task conditions.
released: visibly open manipulating gripper means yes, even close to the object; clearly closed and gripping means no; occluded opening means uncertain. Out-of-view gripper with the object visibly at its target and no visible gripping may be yes. Ignore idle grippers; do not require withdrawal or a release event.
Use uncertainty rather than imagined evidence. Check descriptions against images, correcting errors. Do not certify unobserved intermediate frames.
Return ONLY JSON with fact_checks and checks. fact_checks is a nonempty list of {id:"V1", source_ids:["I1","C1"], status:"supported|corrected|unresolved", evidence:"brief image evidence", views:["initial_head|initial_wrist_left|initial_wrist_right|current_head|current_wrist_left|current_wrist_right"]}. Source IDs must exist in the descriptions; a corrected omitted fact may have empty source_ids. checks has exactly goal_satisfied, released, objects_consistent, robot_structure_consistent; each is {value:"yes|no|uncertain", evidence_ids:["V1"], reason:"brief explanation"}. Every yes/no must cite supported or corrected facts, never unresolved facts. All four must be yes for acceptance; the program computes the decision. Do not output a decision field.
